ajay: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change that prefers smaller kernels for int8, we've seen slow memory growth in KV slabs on long sessions (>12k tokens). Not a spike, but steady over minutes. Anyone else?

maria: saw similar in nightly e2e with the 7B int8 profile. Noticed more page churn on GPU0.

liz: I have a short trace — looks like more frequent small allocations in the slot allocator after quantized projection kernels fire. Posting logs below.

liz: ```
KV: slab_total=348MB -> 612MB over 30m
KV: active_slots=12234 -> 16789
KV: page_evictions=142 -> 198
kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=matmul_int8_small (latency_pref)
```

ajay: interesting. Our batching heuristic also got a tweak around same time (batch_pad_limit lowered). Could be interplay: smaller kernels + tighter batches = more fragmented writes.

tom: quick theory: small-kernel matmul produces more fragmented KV writes because it writes smaller contiguous kv ranges, which defeats our slot coalescer. When slot coalescer expects larger contiguous inserts it leaves holes.

maria: +1. On bf16 runs we don't see as much growth — int8 path seems amplification of fragmentation. Accuracy-wise int8 looked ok but the KV layout patterns differ.

buildbot: perf-bot: collected perf trace 2678904319. flamegraph: https://perf.redwood.local/trace/2678904319 (public to team).

ajay: thanks bot. I sampled a pprof snapshot — hot path is kv_slot_write -> slot_alloc_try_coalesce -> mm_kv_page_touch. Coalesce attempt rate dropped from ~80% to ~45% after change.

liz: here's a minimal repro I ran (local):

```bash
# run long chat with int8 kernels and batching 8
./run_infer --model redwood-7b --quantize int8 --batch-size 8 --kernel-policy latency_pref --session-len 14000 --log-kv=1
```

liz: After ~20 minutes it shows the slab growth log above. If I flip to kernel_policy=balanced the growth slows.

ajay: could be two separate knobs: kernel granularity and batch padding. We should try: (A) keep latency_pref but increase batch_pad_limit, (B) keep small batches but force kernel selection to balanced, and (C) try coalescer improvements.

maria: I'll run A/B matrix on the nightly cluster tomorrow. Will include bf16 control and int8.

tom: short-term mitigation: add a soft throttle that triggers larger batch merging for sessions >8k tokens. That should reduce small write frequency.

liz: also worth checking KV eviction heuristics: if we bias eviction by page-density (prefer evict pages with many holes) we might reclaim fragmentation earlier.

ajay: good call. We should be careful: aggressive eviction hurts latency. Add metric for 'page_hole_ratio' and alert when >0.25.

maria: I'll add the metric and experiment with thresholds.

buildbot: perf-bot: created issue #INF-652 "int8 kernel selection -> kv fragmentation" and linked trace.

ajay: action items:
- maria: run A/B matrix (int8 vs bf16, kernel_policy: latency_pref/balanced/cost_pref, batch_pad: low/medium/high) and upload slab + eviction telemetry (due EOD tomorrow)
- tom: prototype batch-merge soft throttle for long sessions (PR branch: tom/kv-batch-merge)
- liz: try page_hole_ratio metric and simulation of density-biased eviction in the simulator
- ajay: I will validate kernel selector heuristics to avoid choosing micro-kernels when expected contiguous KV writes exceed threshold

liz: note: precision vs memory tradeoff — int8 saves ~2.6x memory in model weights but here KV fragmentation erodes that benefit. We should measure net memory per-session (weights+kv) not just weights.

maria: agreed. I'll report net memory and any accuracy delta observed. If accuracy regresses >0.4% we stop int8 for long sessions.

tom: quick experiment idea: try forcing the runtime to use the larger bf16 kernels but keep quantized activations (hybrid path) — may reduce fragmentation while retaining some memory wins.

ajay: nice. Keep the thread updated. If someone hits a clear repro with a small script we can prioritise a hotfix. :thumbsup:

liz: I'll paste a follow-up repro gist if I get a deterministic run.

maria: uploaded initial matrix results to the perf dashboard (link in issue). early signal: balanced kernel + medium batch_pad gives best net memory profile for int8.

ajay: awesome. we'll sync tomorrow 10am in eng-runtime to decide follow-ups.
